I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 20 years, and I know this land like the back of my hand. My household has four people, but some of them work off-farm, so I am the one who stays to watch the crops. I only went to primary school, so I do not read many new farming books, but I have learned what works by doing it year after year and watching my neighbors.

This year I will keep my wheat-maize rotation. It is the only system that fits our climate and our single well. I cannot afford to try strange new methods because if they fail, my family loses a whole season.

For the winter wheat, I will plant improved seeds on all 5 mu right after the National Day holiday in early October. First I will do rotary tillage to chop up the maize stalks and level the field, because wheat needs a fine seedbed. I will spread compound fertilizer as a base dressing, then topdress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring and again at jointing stage. I have my well, so I will irrigate three times: once before winter so the young plants do not dry out, once at jointing when the wheat is thirsty, and once at heading if the spring is dry. I will spray pesticides twice — once for weeds and once if I see aphids or rust. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize. The summer season is short, so I will not waste time ploughing deep. I will use no-tillage seeding right behind the combine to catch the moisture. Hybrid seed costs more, but it gives me much better yield than traditional seed, so I always buy it. I will fertilize at sowing and side-dress nitrogen at the big-flare stage. I will irrigate twice because summer rainfall is unreliable, and I will spray pesticides three times to control weeds, corn borers, and armyworms that always come in July and August. I expect about 600 kg per mu.
